newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS - Banks left out of euphoric market.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS - Banks left out of euphoric market.

text.p: The banking sector took a beating on Wednesday despite a post-rate hike euphoria spreading in the overall stock market centered on technology issues, analysts said.
But they said it was too early to say if Tuesday's quarter point credit tightening by the Federal Reserve marked an end to bank shares' rally that started in January 1995.

"The rolling, choppy activity near highs in most of these financial stocks, which of course have been ultra-bullish for two years, is indicative of maybe some topping activity," said Brian Belski, a vice president and analyst at Dain Bosworth.
"But it's too early to call them bearish," he added, noting that key support levels had yet to be broken.

Chase Manhattan Corp April 95.0 puts and April 100 calls were among the American Stock Exchange's most actives list, which was otherwise dominated by technology issues like Iomega Corp and Intel Corp.
The April 95 puts had volume of 2,438 contracts and April 100 calls traded 4,203 contracts by late trade. The stock was down 2-1/8 to 99-5/8.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchange (PHLX) banking index was down 10.60 to 599.86 at 1450 CST/2050 GMT.

Robert Rack, a senior research analyst at Cincinnati-based Investment Research Institute, said the 50-day moving average for BKX came in at around 600, providing good support. The index had bounced off the average several times last week.
Rack said the key factor for the banking sector was the bond market.
"Any stabilization in the bond market and you're going to see the banks coming together," he said.
BKX April 600 and 605 calls had relatively good volume of 526 and 366 contracts respectively, while April 595 and 615 puts traded more than 200 each.

Earlier in the day, Raphael Soifer, banking industry analyst for Brown Brothers Harriman, cut his short-term rating on four big banks and Merril Lynch & Co Inc to hold from buy, based on the market's likely reaction to the rate hike.
The four banks were Citicorp, BankAmerica Corp, J.P. Morgan & Co Inc and Chase Manhattan.
Citicorp stock was down 2-1/8 to 113-5/8, BankAmerica was off 2-3/4 to 109-1/4 and J.P. Morgan lost 7/8 to 105-1/2.
Belski at Dain Bosworth noted that virtually all regional and money center banks had similar losses today, indicating the declines were an industry-wide reaction to higher interest rates.
Besides the big Chase activity, Citicorp and BankAmerica options also had relatively healthy flows.
Citicorp April 105 puts had volume of 1,193 contracts, while April 115 to 120 calls and 110 to 120 puts traded a few hundred contracts each.
BankAmerica April 95 puts and calls had turnover of about 800 contracts each, with several other strikes trading 200 to 400 contracts.
